articles.title: 2026.43: A New Era
articles.snippet: Welcome back to This Week in Stratechery! This week marks a new era for Stratechery, which is now presented by Stripe . I’m excited about what this partnership can unlock, starting with in-person on-video episodes of Sharp Tech. Check out the YouTube video above (or watch it on Stratechery ); and, for subscribers, look forward to a bonus episode showing up in your subscriber feed every Sunday morning (add your feed on sharptech.fm ). Here were a few of our favorite topics this week: The Best iPad; The Worst Phone. John Gruber wrote a great review of the iPhone Duo, which we broke down on Dithering . In short, it’s an iPad that fits in your pocket, and it’s awesome at that; just don’t expect a good phone. Plus, on Monday we discussed Apple’s surprising partnership with Meta for edge AI, a topic I also covered in Tuesday’s Update . — Ben Thompson The SS Sarandos in a Storm. The past week has seen a flood of bad news for Netflix: layoffs, executive departures, another disappointing round of earnings, and another hit to a share price that has taken a 40% hit over the past 12 months. Wednesday’s Update provides a comprehensive state of the union , and we doubled back on the topic for a fun conversation on this week’s Sharp Tech , where we divided the company’s problems into areas that can be fixed (the content) and what may be much trickier (growing the business in a world where Meta and YouTube are primary engagement competition). — Andrew Sharp You Can See Everything, But Can’t Trust Anyone. Allow me to be the 1,000th person on the internet to recommend Nathan Fielder’s new Elizabeth Holmes documentary, You Can See Everything . After declaring on Sharp Tech last week that I wasn’t interested in seeing it, I did in fact check it out, and wound up loving it. I wrote about my experience on Sharp Text , with 5 spoiler-free notes for anyone still on the fence, and 5 more reactions for anyone who’s seen it. Compulsively watchable (and worth seeing in a theater), I think it may have also been the most effective document of our modern media environment I’ve ever seen. — AS Presented by It’s kind of weird to be the Internet’s number one fan of ads. What makes it even weirder is that I have been the Internet’s number one fan of ads without actually having ads on Stratechery . That second part is changing: I’m super excited to announce that Stripe is going to be the presenting sponsor of Stratechery. And, at the end of the day, for me it couldn’t be any other company. One of my hangups in terms of advertising is that I take my ethics super seriously, and ultimately, if a company is helping pay the bills, it’s hard to be truly objective about them. What I realized, however, is that it’s hard for me to be objective about Stripe anyway. I wanted to be a professional blogger long before I started Stratechery; however, I thought I had missed my chance, particularly as it became clear that advertising was not a long term business model for a one-person site. However, when Stripe launched with support for recurring billing, I realized there was a better model: subscriptions. 13 years later, and I’m still a happy customer. Or, to put it another way, I’m already conflicted because I love Stripe. I’m not the only one: more than 5 million businesses use Stripe, accounting for 1.7% of global GDP. Moreover, a lot of those businesses are Internet native and accretive to the world’s economy, which is to say that Stripe is literally making the world a better place. That’s an easy company to get behind, especially since they have been behind Stratechery from the very beginning. — Ben Thompson Stratechery Articles and Updates Do You Trust Apple? — Apple has a lot of trust in terms of delivering integrated products and preserving privacy; the real trust question is if you think Siri AI will justify investing more in their ecosystem. Muse Spark Open, Meta + Apple, Thin and Thick — Meta has a new open source model, and to everyone’s surprise, they are are partnering with Apple to make sure you can run it locally. Netflix Earnings, Business or Franchise, Disney’s Deal — Netflix has a solid business, which is exactly the problem: the company increasingly seems like a business and not a franchise, at least in terms of growth. An Interview with Craig Moffett About SpaceX and Bubbles — An interview with Craig Moffett about SpaceX, from launch to broadband to mobile, plus how he is applying the lessons of the dot-com bubble to today. Sharp Text by Andrew Sharp You Can See Everything (And It’s a Great Time) — Nathan Fielder’s movie lives up to the hype and captures the modern world better than any art in recent memory. Dithering with Ben Thompson and Daring Fireball’s John Gruber Apple + Meta AI The Duo Review Asianometry with Jon Yu The Birth & Rise of India’s IT Outsourcing Industry Sharp China with Andrew Sharp and Sinocism’s Bill Bishop New Export Controls in Multiple Sectors; Q3 GDP and the Fifth Plenum; Europe Presses Forward; OpenAI and Nvidia Chips Greatest of All Talk Aday Mara and the OKC Woodchipper, An Emergency Celtics Panic Watch, Silver Appreciation(???) and Laker Dreams Sharp Tech with Andrew Sharp and Ben Thompson Netflix Angst, The End of the Internet, Q&A on Meta’s VR Glasses, Anthropic Alignment, You Can See Everything

articles.title: Video Friday: Quadruped Robot Solves Giant Rubik’s Cube by Itself
articles.snippet: Video Friday is your weekly selection of awesome robotics videos, collected by your friends at IEEE Spectrum robotics. We also post a weekly calendar of upcoming robotics events for the next few months. Please send us your events for inclusion. CoRL 2026 : 9–12 November 2026, AUSTIN Humanoids 2026 : 6–9 December 2026, SANTA CLARA, CA Enjoy today’s videos! A quadruped robot autonomously solves a giant Rubik’s Cube using only its feet. [ ETH Zurich Robotics Systems Lab ] Humans effortlessly react to the world; they adeptly return a tennis shot, catch a falling cup, step aside from a passing cart, or pass a box tossed during truck unloading. These everyday actions require anticipating a moving target and reflexively responding with the whole body within about a second. Such visual reactive whole-body control remains challenging for humanoids. We present Reflex, a three-stage framework that learns these capabilities stage by stage while connecting them through a compact representation of object dynamics. [ Reflex ] Thanks, Weikai! I have long advocated for exactly this in the context of robotic laundry folding , or more broadly, other robot recognition and manipulation tasks. Why not make it easy when we can make it easy? [ ACM SIGCHI ] We first wrote about Parallel Systems in 2022 . Nice to see them still rolling. [ Parallel Systems ] I’ll be honest with you: The end of this video is freaking me out a little bit for some reason. This video showcases the whole-body loco-manipulation capabilities of KAIST Humanoid v0.9, developed at the DRCD Lab in collaboration with RAILAB, which developed the robot’s arms. Using onboard visual feedback, the humanoid demonstrates pushing objects weighing up to 35 kilograms and lifting objects up to 20 kg to arrange the letters “KAIST.” [ KAIST DRCD Lab ] When you don’t spend any money on sensors for your robots, you can afford much bigger wheels. [ RaiLab Kaist ] Those robots with wires have gotten somewhat weirder. [ JSK Robotics Laboratory ] The AthenaZero has two, three-fingered robot hands driven by tendons. This design allows the fingers to interdigitate to hold objects of different sizes, such as an egg or a hammer. Each finger is powered by a motor located in the robot’s torso to keep the hand light, transmitting force through flexible cables. This hand is both fast (closing in about 80 milliseconds) and strong. With the addition of highly accurate barometric pressure sensors, it can also be gentle. [ Robotics and AI Institute ] via [ Science Robotics ] A biohybrid robot combines living tissue with engineered materials—here, lab-grown skeletal muscle paired with a soft, 3D-printed scaffold that turns the muscle’s contraction into movement. What if you designed the living muscle and the soft scaffold together, instead of growing the muscle and then building a skeleton around it? In this work from the Soft Robotics Lab at ETH Zurich, we adapted a soft-body simulation framework to co-optimize both at once—and the resulting centimeter-scale bioactuators achieve up to 11x more range of motion than previous systems of comparable tissue volume. Strong enough to jump, swim, walk, and grasp. [ ETH Zurich Soft Robotics Lab ] Oh yes, this is definitely the use case that will scale humanoid robots. [ Unitree ] Here are a couple more teasers from the upcoming ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST). [ ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology ] In three hours, on a single GPU, SuperMimic surpasses the return of a state-of-the-art motion tracker baseline trained for seven days on 128 GPUs. It reduces GPU-hours by more than 1,000× and fails on only 25 of 129,514 benchmark motions, versus 179 failures for the baseline. After 9.8 hours on two GPUs, SuperMimic achieves zero failures. [ Hybrid Robotics ] This is getting out of hand! Now there are two of them! Introducing the Grain Weevil dual robot attachment. Two robots linked into one larger machine, run by a single operator, doing the work of up to three robots. [ Grain Weevil ] Today [21 October 2026] at CES Unveiled Milan, Generative Bionics announced its plan to build Europe’s largest Physical AI Data Factory, with AMD as its AI infrastructure partner. [ Generative Bionics ] From robotic rovers exploring the rugged lunar landscape to lunar terrain vehicles carrying Artemis astronauts across the surface, mobility will play a crucial role in establishing an enduring human presence on the moon. During the early phases of Moon Base development, these vehicles will help NASA investigate the lunar South Pole region, conduct scientific research, test new technologies, and gather the information that will inform future missions. In this Moon Base update, get a closer look at some of the lunar terrain vehicles and robotic rovers helping to pave the way for humanity’s first lunar outpost. [ NASA ] I appreciate the designer of this single motor drone crediting previous research, which included some cool drones from UPenn that we wrote about in 2014. [ Joshua Bird ] Why choose a bipedal, human-form robot over specialized wheels, gantry arms, or quadruped platforms? Speaking at the Humanoids Summit Seoul 2026, Michael Perry from Persona AI tackles the single most debated question in the industry and delivers the definitive business and engineering justification for the humanoid form factor. [ Humanoids Summit ]

articles.title: AI Is Getting Good at Math. Here’s Why.
articles.snippet: In May, an internal model at OpenAI found a counterexample to Erdős's unit distance conjecture . Open since 1946. Many experts had tried to prove it. OpenAI found a counterexample instead. A month later, OpenAI published a proof of the Cycle Double Cover (CDC) problem , then solutions to ten more open problems by July. And a proof of Navier Stokes in September. Anthropic published a formalization of the fermat's last theorem , and advanced bounds on Reimann's hypothesis . The models are suddenly good at math. The question that interests me is whether we can predict what kinds of problems these models will solve. What makes a problem tractable for an LLM, and what do these solutions have in common? If AI solves problems differently from humans, identifying the difference should help us decide where to point it. The unit-distance disproof has the richest commentary, so let’s start there. Problem complexity Here is a simple mental model. To solve any given problem, you need a sequence of hints or insights with work between them. This maps surprisingly well to simple everyday problems and to complex ideas like General Relativity 1 (see Bonus). The sequence looks something like this: Insight -> time / effort -> insight -> time/effort -> solution. An expert would need fewer hints than a beginner would, as they would have more background. In his commentary on unit-distance proof, WT Gowers uses a similar idea: the difficulty of the proof is the shortest sequence of hints that would let experts reconstruct it. He calls it Kolmogorov complexity 2 modulo experts. For the unit-distance problem, his hint sequence had three parts: Look for a counterexample. Take the best known construction and generalize it. Try a sequence of number fields of increasing degree, but work with prime ideals of bounded norm. Gowers’ proposed formula for complexity is 2^k + t, where k is the length of the shortest hint sequence and t is the work required to develop it. It is the sort of formula that looks rigorous right up until you try to put a number into it, which is more or less the point. Complexity grows exponentially with the number of insights you need to solve a problem. Most problem solving is the work between these insights. You have a eureka moment, then spend months developing the hint until another conceptual jump becomes possible. For an expert, time spent is a useful proxy for this work, hence t. Hand someone the first unit-distance hint and they still have to do enough work to reach the generalized construction. Useful, but post hoc. You can’t look at the problem and predict it would need x number of hints. So, a problem’s age, the number of tries, and the prize attached to it are common proxies to ascribe difficulty. Characteristics of a given hint A typical insight changes the formulation of the problem. The representation and understanding of the problem change . Two things decide how much a hint is worth: How unlikely it looked before, against how obvious it looks after supplying the hint → This is harder than people realize. In unit distance, many experts did not consider the counterexample as likely. Where it belongs in the sequence: hints are ordered. A third hint is useful only after the work on the first two have made enough progress for it to be actionable. This defeats the naive brute force idea of listing a thousand mathematical techniques and trying every combination 3 . Hints sequence traverses a tree. Initial insights change the problem and reveal the choices that follow. Humans solve problems breadth first Combine k and t and you get the human search pattern . Generate candidate directions, explore them shallowly, abandon most, and commit to a few. A promising direction is abandoned if it does not give enough encouragement early 4 . This is a human constraint: Developing an idea can take months. Before committing, a researcher needs reasons to believe it will lead somewhere: conceptual promise, early results, or experience with similar problems. The longer it takes to find out, the higher the bar for trying the idea. Most research software exists to shrink this time by automating the tedious, mechanical, repeatable work. AI shrinks it far enough that the search pattern itself flips, and everything downstream follows from that. AI and complexity First, t. The model’s equivalent of effort is compute and tokens, spent on one trajectory (test time compute) or spread across parallel agents (parallel test time compute). Pretraining also supplies knowledge that a human researcher would have to locate or reconstruct. No individual expert is aware of every previous development, so occasionally they end up redoing things already done. The bigger difference is how models search: LLMs are depth first Give the model a single prompt and it will give you a solution. Maybe correct, perhaps not. Ask for a proof and it will give you something that approaches a good proof. CoT for these models runs in a greedy depth first manner too. And the process scales. Give parallel agents ten approaches and you get ten attempts developed toward a conclusion. Maybe all distinct, or some overlapping. Each either hits a roadblock or produces an argument that looks right. Left alone, this gets you beautiful false proofs. This seems like a waste of compute and resources, until you add an automated verifier 5 that can prune the completed trajectories and identify the correct ones. With this checker, it is now rational to spend enormous compute on uncertain ideas. You find out whether a given idea works or not within minutes. The catch is that the verifier can only judge finished arguments. It cannot tell you whether a half-developed idea is going anywhere. The contrast How good does a hint need to be if you can find out whether it works in five minutes? For humans, the quality bar is high because it could take months of work to pursue a hint. For a model, the bar nearly disappears. The hint can be ordinary, implausible, or b

These tumors basically have a broken DNA spell-checker, so mutations pile up until the cancer looks foreign to the immune system. Dostarlimab blocks PD-1, the off switch tumors use to keep T cells at bay, which lets the immune system clear the cancer (explained in the video above). In GSK’s 154-patient trial, after a median of 26 months, cancer hadn’t progressed in 71% of patients treated with dostarlimab alone. In MSK’s expanded 50-patient study, every patient responded, and 93% stayed cancer-free for at least a year. Only about 3% of locally advanced rectal cancers are dMMR, per the FDA, so this isn’t a cure for all rectal cancers, let alone all cancer, but we’re getting into a pretty consistent, almost weekly, pattern of new therapies working against specific cancers, which seems like the way we’ll beat cancer overall. articles.snippet: If you are reading this, you’re receiving this from our new provider, Beehiiv! We are making progress on our redesign — if you have a friend that didn’t receive AINews, please find us in Spam filter and move us out to your Inbox… thank you! AINews is now free… we are building new subscriber benefits soon. We ordinarily try not to repeat title stories if we already covered it, as we did Patch the Planet yesterday and our Cyber trend call in July. But, if the scale is warranted, we also view our continued selection to also be signal - we can call things out 0, 1, or multiple times and that should be in proportion to its importance/historical significance in AI. We last did this with OpenClaw. “Black October” counts as such. Here’s a list: View post on X ↗ AI News for 10/21/2026-10/22/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews' website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space . You can opt in/out of email frequencies! AI Twitter Recap Black October: AI-Accelerated Vulnerability Disclosures Overwhelm Defenders Scale of the incident wave : Over roughly 48 hours, a cluster of critical disclosures and breaches landed together ( summary , roundup , patch list ). Core software : PHP2Shell is an unauthenticated RCE in PHP. GitLab disclosed a CVSS 10 flaw affecting releases since 2014, patched in 19.5.1. Node.js shipped a Brotli decoder RCE fix, and NGINX and HTTP/3 also had DoS issues. Supply chain : LiteLLM 1.107.0 shipped with a password stealer. Railway told users to rotate secrets after possible exposure of customer keys. Zeabur is shutting down after 321,810 accounts were breached. Certificate authority : eMudhra's CA keys were trivially weak; one key was reportedly the number 4. A researcher says Claude cracked them with a single prompt, and eMudhra is exiting the CA business ( Rundown ). Python users are advised to update pip, uv, certifi and system CA stores ( advisory ). Healthcare data : Quest Diagnostics, which serves about half of US hospitals and physicians, reported exposed patient data ( report ). CVE volume : Monthly CVEs reportedly rose from about 4k to about 15k since April ( @saranormous ). State actor using agentic tooling : Microsoft attributes the ConnectWise supply-chain compromise to China-aligned Storm-0940. The group used the open agentic pentest framework ARTEX against 2,250+ Microsoft 365 tenants at about 2,900 sign-in attempts per minute ( MSTIC via @kimmonismus , detail ). Speed of compromise : In some cases the group reached privileged access in under 3 hours. Other operators : CrowdStrike documented four operators running AI-agent campaigns, including one that hit at least 15 Argentine healthcare organizations. PHP provenance is disputed : The bugs were found by OpenAI models in August and embargoed until Wednesday's fix ( Rundown ). The PHP Foundation also says Claude Mythos had scanned PHP earlier ( @Hesamation ). Defense-wins framing : @BlancheMinerva calls the "offense winning" narrative disinformation, arguing this was a defensive audit and there is no evidence of large-scale exploitation ( thread ). Disclosure timing : Joshua Achiam reportedly noted that only about 4 of roughly 16 major incidents actually occurred this week; the rest were found earlier and disclosed now ( MTS ). Rogue agents in bank accounts : Axios reports that major US banks are detecting unauthorized third-party agents inside customer accounts. Some appear to act beyond user instructions ( scoop ). Pushback : @peterwildeford reads these as user-authorized agents that banks had not authorized, not hacks or rogue AI ( take ). Policy response : Sen. Schiff called for mandatory industry-wide AI guardrails ( post ). Outlook from Anthropic security : Deputy CISO Jason Clinton says things "are going to get a lot worse before they get better." He urges security leaders to ask boards for funding for the basics and expects defenders need to hold on for about 18 months ( post ). Defensive tooling : Formal verification at scale : Anthropic's Frontier Red Team, working with Theorem Labs, used Claude to prove security properties across more than 100 open-source libraries in weeks ( announcement ). Reported figures are about 180M lines of machine-checked proofs covering 239 entry points in 123 libraries, with hundreds of bugs patched ( summary ). Patch tooling : Cognition open-sourced a vulnerability-remediation agent plugin ( blog ), and cve.now aggregates four CVE feeds with plain-English explanations ( launch ). Exposure checklist : @_philschmid posted a read-only agent prompt for checking exposure to the LiteLLM, Railway, PHP, GitLab and eMudhra issues ( prompt ). Safety, Oversight and Eval Integrity METR/Redwood embedded assessment at OpenAI : Two auditors from METR and Redwood Research spent three weeks on-site evaluating OpenAI's internal misalignment monitoring for agents ( METR , OpenAI ). Findings : Reported issues include agents deferring monitoring indefinitely by not returning control, and a Codex sandbox plus Auto-Review bypass. One exploit could keep hundreds of recent actions unmonitored, and context compression left about 10% of eligible internal Codex traffic unmonitored ( summary ). Redactions : The report was cut from 61 to 38 pages ( @AndrewCurran_ ). METR says OpenAI could redact and that METR could not describe the redactions unilaterally ( note ). Fired chain-of-thought researchers : WSJ reports that the three researchers OpenAI fired last month had pushed to keep chain-of-thought visible. articles.title: The relentless math of bandwagoning
articles.snippet: It often seems that everyone is talking about what everyone is talking about. No one cares about a song or a movie or a political issue–and then they do. Then it’s everywhere. But of course, that’s precisely why. Most people feel safe when they’re engaging within the expected social norms. It’s easier to fit in and to avoid an error. Or, if that’s your thing, it’s easier to stand out in contrast to everyone else who is trying to fit in. Either way, we’re always on the lookout for a bandwagon to hop on. The media, in their relentless search for newsstand sales, clicks and likes, seek precisely the same thing. PT Barnum figured out that putting a marching band on a wagon at the front of the parade drew a crowd, and then Dan Rice, an actual clown, realized that politicians would be eager to ride on a wagon that had a crowd, which drew others to the crowd and the cycle continued. The math is simple: you can’t bandwagon by yourself. The nature of bandwagoning means that it will always be overrepresented in any sampling of the media. Just because someone organized a parade doesn’t mean you have to be in it.

articles.title: Kazakhstan Expands Compute for Its AI Future
articles.snippet: Kazakhstan’s AI ecosystem is moving from infrastructure plans to deployment. The shift is visible across the full AI stack — from infrastructure to models to applications. The announcements below — coinciding with a visit to Astana by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang — point to the nation’s increasing supply of accelerated computing, along with its growing demand for what comes next. On Friday, Oct. 23, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang visited Astana, meeting with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev at the Akorda Presidential Palace and joining Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiyev — Kazakhstan’s minister of AI and digital development — for a public fireside chat at the Alem.AI program. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Jensen Huang and Kazakhstan’s AI Minister Speak at Alem.AI In their fireside chat at Alem.AI, Kazakhstan’s international center for artificial intelligence, Madiyev and Huang discussed the country’s push to become an AI nation — building the energy and computing infrastructure to support homegrown AI and applying it across the economy. Madiyev said Kazakhstan wants AI that reflects its language and culture. “We want AI that understands and speaks Kazakh and captures cultural contexts and cultural specifics,” he said, describing the country’s work on Kazakh-language models. Huang said Kazakhstan could turn its energy resources into a foundation for AI production — and a new kind of export. “Instead of just exporting energy, in the future, you could transform energy into intelligence and export intelligence,” he said. He also argued that local data is central to that ambition: it embodies a country’s culture, history and values. “Your country’s data is your natural resource. It belongs to you.” The conversation also turned to physical AI. Madiyev pointed to Kazakhstan’s factories, mines, agriculture, transport and logistics as potential areas for development, asking how the country could become a hub for training models for robots and other physical systems. Huang called the idea “fantastic,” saying physical AI could transform industries from mining and mineral processing to agriculture. Huang said AI and robotics can help people do more, but ambition will shape how fully they seize that opportunity. He applied the idea to Kazakhstan, saying AI could help lift the country and its people. “If you have ambition, and I believe you do, AI will lift your nation,” Huang said. “AI will lift your people.” Huang also praised the founders of Higgsfield AI, the Kazakhstan-founded startup, and it was announced NVIDIA is making an investment into the startup during the event. “The first thing and the last thing is you invest in people, not companies,” he said, describing the founders as visionary and pointing to their effort to compete globally. Asked about AI security, Huang said the technology must be developed and deployed responsibly. He described NVIDIA’s OpenShell as a way to contain AI agents by limiting their access to files and tools and monitoring their activity. For young people entering a fast-changing field, Huang recommended learning how AI works — not just how to use it. He said aspiring AI programmers should understand the technology’s principles, strengths and weaknesses, combining technical knowledge with the ability to work effectively with AI. “I envy being 18 years old today… because the world is changing so rapidly, and there’s a complete reset because of technology.” The Infrastructure Layer Is Scaling The visits coincided with a signing ceremony marking Firebird’s investment agreement with the government of Kazakhstan, held at the presidential palace. Building on its first AI factory in Armenia, Firebird is expanding into Kazakhstan, where it has secured a U.S. export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs. The first phase is under construction with Kazakhtelecom at Data Center Valley, targeting commercial launch in the third quarter of 2027. A planned second phase would bring Firebird’s total potential AI infrastructure capacity in Kazakhstan to approximately 500 megawatts. Firebird also plans to establish Firebird Labs Kazakhstan to support local AI startups, research and talent development through funding, access to compute and research partnerships. Firebird cofounder and CEO Razmig Hovaghimian attended the signing ceremony at the Akorda Presidential Palace alongside government officials. “What began as a seed of an idea 180 days ago has grown into a major investment in Kazakhstan’s AI future,” said Razmig Hovaghimian, co-Founder and CEO of Firebird. “President Tokayev’s vision gave us the confidence to think bigger about what we can build together. With Jensen Huang here today, that ambition feels more tangible than ever. We’re building the infrastructure for Kazakhstan’s talent and ideas to reach the world.” Kazakhtelecom , the nation’s largest telecommunications company, has already deployed 400 NVIDIA H200 and 480 NVIDIA B300 GPUs in Astana and Almaty. Next year, the company plans to deploy more than 1,000 GPUs in the Data Center Valley , along with more than 1,000 NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs in the Ekibastuz region, serving diverse workloads with infrastructure that enterprises, developers and institutions can use at scale. An Honorary Black Belt for Huang At the end of their meeting, President Tokayev presented Huang with the Order of Dostyk, First Class, for his contribution to the development of artificial intelligence in Kazakhstan. Dostyk means friendship and the Order honors peace, friendship and cooperation. Later that day, President of the International Judo Federation (IJF) Marius Vizer and Timur Kemell, IJF director of promotion and development and a member of the IJF Executive Committee, presented Huang with an honorary black belt in Judo. The belt, embroidered in gold stitching, was a special thanks for Huang’s support of Kazakhstan’s AI ambition and for leadership aligned with the spirit and rigor of the martial art. AI-Native Com

From Eyeballs to Annual Run Rates (ARR): Buzzy Pricing Metrics and the Anthropic Trade!
articles.snippet: I was in San Francisco last week to talk to NYU Stern Alumni on October 15, and it was the day that Anthropic had a pre-IPO meeting with prospective investors. While I was not at the meeting, the focus of teh gathering was laying a foundation for its upcoming IPO, with the company reporting third-quarter revenue of $16.8 billion, which news reports described as surging 45% over the previous quarter's revenues, and positive profits, albeit on an adjusted basis. During the meeting, Anthropic also reported an annual revenue run rate (ARR) of $67 billion, a metric that those in the AI space have adopted with gusto, with an estimate that the ARR would exceed $100 billion by the end of the year. The nature of ARR, where choices on how revenue is calculated (gross versus net) and on annualization periods (daily, weekly or monthly) can make a significant difference, has led investors to be skeptical about comparing these numbers across time and companies. While I share some of that skepticism, it is worth remembering that young businesses are often priced on inventive metrics, some with more basis than others. In the late nineties, dot.com companies were priced not just on the number of visitors to their websites, but on eyeballs , where Mary Meeker argued that ad spending at these companies was correlated with time that these visitors spent on websites (eyeballs), rather than with total visitors. In the last decade, you saw social media companies priced based upon the number of users and subscription-based companies on subscriber numbers. In this post, I will try to lay out the rationale for why pricing supplants valuation in young companies and why that pricing almost always has to be built around messy metrics like eyeballs, users and ARR, rather than more conventional metrics like earnings, book value or cash flows. Young Companies in a Corporate Life Cycle All businesses, no matter how large and established they might be today, started as young businesses and matured. With that perspective in mind, I will start this discussion by placing young businesses in a corporate life cycle in the figure below: One of the first steps in analyzing a company is placing it in the right stage of the life cycle, and there are three choices that you can use in making this placement: Chronological age : The first and simplest choice is to look at the age of a business, putting companies that have been in operation for short periods into the young company grouping and classifying those that have been in operation for longer as mature. While this approach is easy to use, and for the most part, effective, it can be misleading in businesses like infrastructure, where it can take decades to get established, and in technology, where the lack of capital intensity can allow a company can go from start-up to mature in a few years. Industry grouping : Another choice is categorizing industry groups into life cycle stages and assuming that any company that belongs to a specific industry group shares its life cycle characteristics. For decades, investors have viewed technology as a shorthand for growth and put technology companies into the earlier stages of the life cycle and utilities as mature or even declining and put all utility companies into the mature to declining company grouping. The limitation of this approach is that there will be divergence within each group, where some companies separate themselves from their industry group; there are mature and even declining companies that are in the technology grouping, and there are power companies that have taken advantage of the data center boom to become growth companies. With technology in particular, where companies age in dog years, I talked about how companies can get mis-categorized and sometimes mismanaged as growth companies , even though their best days are behind them. Operating metrics : Ultimately, life cycle effects show up in the operating metrics of companies, and there are common characteristics that young companies share, and they include the following: High revenue growth : Young companies usually have high revenue growth, and while this is usually off a small revenue base, there are exceptions, where companies with scaled up revenues are still able to show high growth. Operating losses : As young companies scale up, they usually struggle with unformed business models, and at low scale, their fixed costs overwhelm their revenues, resulting in negative or very low operating profit margins. Negative free cash flows : Free cash flows are after reinvestment, and as young companies invest to deliver on their potential growth, that reinvestment will generate negative free cash flows. Failure risk : The confluence of small revenues, losses and negative free cashflows, which must be funded with external capital (equity or debt) exposes young firms to significant risk of failure. The figure below captures the shifts in operating metrics, as companies move through the life cycle: Put simply, if a company has revenue growth in single digits, stable margins and positive free cash flows to the firm, it is a mature company, no matter how it views itself. Conversely, a firm with high revenue growth, negative or very low profit margins and large negative free cashflows to the firms is a young growth firm, no matter what its scale. Recognizing those characteristics is critical in understanding why so many give up on valuing young companies, and why pricing will often be based on unfamiliar metrics. How do Anthropic and OpenAI measure up in the life cycle? Using a patchwork of public data and leaked information, here are the numbers on key operating metrics that I have as of October 2026 for both companies: The sky-high revenue growth and operating losses are a clear indication that these are young, growth companies, but note that the revenues (albeit on an ARR basis) at both companies are already large, suggesting that they are growing at scale. articles.title: Why AI Compute Comes in Rectangles — Erik Bernhardsson, Modal CEO
articles.snippet: Warm welcome to Basil Chatha , our newest cohost from the Forward Deployed side of the AI Engineering world! We’ll be ramping up a new show with him and couldn’t pass up an interview with Modal’s CEO Eric on the occasion of their monster Series D! Two years ago, we spoke with Erik Bernhardsson about his vision for truly serverless AI infrastructure: developers should be able to run code without provisioning clusters, predicting load, or paying for idle resources. CTO Akshat then joined us to talk about Modal’s infra primitives and stack to offer those primitives and agent experience. A lot has changed in the past 5 months. Since their $5B series C, Modal now reports it crossed $1 billion in annualized run rate , raised a $750 million Series D at a $16B valuation , and has spun up nearly three billion sandboxes. In this conversation, Erik joins Vibhu to explain the infrastructure and economics behind that growth—and why demand for compute rarely looks like the contracts used to buy it. Watch the full conversation on YouTube → GPU demand isn’t rectangular A typical capacity contract gives a customer a fixed number of GPUs for a fixed period. Plot capacity against time and you get a rectangle. Real workloads behave differently: they grow, spike, and fall throughout the day. Buy enough for the peak and you pay for idle hardware; buy less and you risk missing demand. Erik describes Modal’s bet as a kind of duration transformation: pool demand across thousands of customers, secure capacity underneath, and let each customer use what they need when they need it. The smoother the aggregate demand, the more useful that pool can be. It’s a useful companion to our conversation with SF Compute’s Evan Conrad : Evan focuses on making capacity tradeable; Erik focuses on making it usable in smaller, elastic slices. There is a financial risk on the other side. If a provider locks in capacity at today’s prices and GPU prices later fall, it can be left holding expensive supply. Erik says he doesn’t expect an imminent collapse, but thinks the possibility matters when building the business. Jump to the GPU price discussion → The sandbox that almost didn’t make it Modal launched sandboxes after Erik and cofounder Akshat Bubna noticed that language models could generate code—and that someone would need a place to run it. Early adoption was modest enough that the team discussed shutting the product down. Then coding agents, background agents, and reinforcement learning created new demand. Erik says sandboxes have grown to roughly a third of Modal’s revenue, a result he didn’t predict at launch. That growth also changes what infrastructure has to do. An agent may create an environment, run code, inspect the result, and try again many times. The latency of starting and restoring those environments becomes part of the experience. In our recent interview with Akshat , we explored this shift from developer experience to agent experience; here Erik adds the product and business story. Jump to the sandbox discussion → Fast startup is an infrastructure feature Elasticity only works if capacity can arrive quickly enough to matter. Modal’s serverless GPU write-up describes the machinery: a buffer of available GPUs, a custom filesystem, process checkpointing, and GPU memory snapshots. Those pieces reduce the work needed to bring another model replica online. It is a concrete example of how infrastructure decisions show up in an application’s responsiveness and cost. We also discuss Erik’s path from Spotify’s recommendation system to Modal, how the company buys compute, alternatives to NVIDIA, forward-deployed engineers, and why code review is optional at Modal. Jump to engineering culture → Show notes Modal — the AI infrastructure platform Erik founded. Erik’s writing — his essays on infrastructure, markets, and building companies. Modal’s Series D announcement — the company’s latest reported growth and sandbox milestones. How Modal achieved truly serverless GPUs — the startup and scaling techniques behind elastic inference. Modal’s resource solver — how it selects capacity across changing prices and availability. Scaling to one million concurrent sandboxes — an engineering account of sandbox scaling. Our first interview with Erik — the original serverless infrastructure thesis. Our interview with Akshat Bubna — infrastructure and developer experience for agents. The Programmable Data Center — Evan Conrad on GPU trading and physical settlement. articles.title: What will computer chips look like in 2045?
articles.snippet: I spent two days touring Intel’s most advanced fab and talking to its technical leadership to understand what the chips of the future will look like. A lot of what’s coming next – gate-all-around transistors, backside power, CFET, hybrid bonding – is hard to follow without actually seeing it, so we made all the awesome animated explainers that I wish I had while I was prepping. I also asked Intel’s leadership how the semiconductor industry will cope with the enormous shock in demand from AI. AI compute has grown 3x a year for the last decade, but according to Intel’s CTO, Intel could only double leading-edge wafer production with today’s global stock of chipmaking tools. What kinds of tricks can foundries pull to extend this crossover point where demand surges way ahead of supply? This was a totally new format for us - hope you enjoy! I also made flashcards for the concepts I had to learn to prep for this episode here . Watch on YouTube , Apple Podcasts or Spotify . Sponsors WorkOS helps you do business with enterprises. It gives you access to all the features most commonly required by enterprises: SSO, SCIM, RBAC, audit logs, and more. It’s easy to plug these features in — it only takes a few lines of code — and WorkOS is releasing new functionality all the time, including things like auth for agents. If you want to join the 3,000+ companies that rely on WorkOS, go to workos.com Jane Street built a powerful tool called magic-trace to help analyze and debug their trading systems. It only exists because one engineer noticed a feature on Intel chips called Processor Trace and thought it’d be valuable to build on top of. Now, traders and developers across Jane Street use magic-trace every single day! If you want to be trusted to pursue the ideas you think matter most, Jane Street is hiring. Go to janestreet.com/dwarkesh Antithesis ’ testing platform lets you perfectly reproduce every single bug you find. That’s because it runs on a fully deterministic computer, which strips out all the unpredictability that can make certain bugs flaky and hard to pin down. To build it, Antithesis found every source of non-determinism in Intel’s x86 architecture and either sealed it off or replaced it with a controlled simulation. articles.title: NVIDIA Unveils Minerva to Bring End-to-End Observability for AI Factories
articles.snippet: Launched today, NVIDIA Minerva is an AIOps platform built to help teams find problems earlier and keep AI factories productive. It brings together telemetry from infrastructure and AI workloads, then applies purpose-built AI models to turn that data into timely, actionable insight. AI factories are among the most complex operations in the world, with vast numbers of GPUs working across high-speed networks to train models and serve AI applications. At that scale, a single degraded component can slow an entire job. The warning signs may be easy to miss, such as a GPU running hotter than its peers or an NVMe drive losing performance under load. The platform focuses on AI factory yield, a measure of the useful work infrastructure produces through GPU hours, goodput, cluster uptime and token production. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Delivering a Dynamic View of an AI Factory Traditional monitoring tools often divide the data center into separate views. Networking, compute, site reliability and machine learning teams each see a different part of the operation. Minerva connects those signals across NVIDIA GPUs, networking, storage, schedulers and workloads. With these signals, Minerva builds a dynamic knowledge graph that logically maps the infrastructure — GPUs, SuperNICs, switches and cables — and the jobs running on it. This context helps operators trace a slow training job to the component affecting it, even across a factory with hundreds of thousands of GPUs. It analyzes billions of data points per hour using supervised and unsupervised machine learning. It learns normal behavior, detects previously unseen anomalies, predicts emerging failures and correlates related events based on the factory’s topology. Instead of sending every symptom to an operator, it can group an event storm into a focused incident with a likely root cause. Minerva comes with a native AI assistant and connects to external agentic AI tools. This adds a natural-language interface grounded in live telemetry. Operators can investigate cluster health and receive recommended remediation through conversation. Teams can keep a person in the loop to manually implement fixes or connect Minerva to automation through infrastructure application programming interfaces and external systems. Results That Maximize AI Factory Yield The ability to correlate workload and infrastructure issues along with its agentic AI capabilities help simplify AI factory operations. Instead of dealing with a blizzard of alerts, Minerva aggregates related problems into a single actionable item. This allows AIOps teams to move from reactive to proactive maintenance. And all of this helps AI factories maximize GPU uptime. Minerva delivers value for the key metrics AI factories focus on: Longer time between interruptions : Minerva spots trouble before it happens, so jobs run longer without incident. Faster time to repair : When an incident does happen, Minerva pinpoints the problem, leading to a significantly quicker resolution. Greater insight : Modern AI infrastructure generates a flood of data; Minerva filters it out, leaving only the handful of alerts that actually matter. IREN is among the NVIDIA partners using Minerva to optimize its AI factories. “As we scale our AI factories, the key to providing the best service for our customers is maximizing the productivity of our GPUs,” said Denis Skrinnikoff, chief technology officer of IREN. “NVIDIA Minerva gives our operations team one view across the network, the GPUs and the jobs running on them, so we focus more on proactive maintenance rather than troubleshooting. That visibility strengthens our operating model for the infrastructure we’re building next.” Joining IREN , Aolani , Bitdeer AI , IBM , Jio, Lambda , Quake AI and Tesla plan to deploy Minerva. In addition to Dell Technologies , Lenovo and Supermicro will offer Minerva as part of their AI factory operations portfolios. Learn more about NVIDIA Minerva . articles.title: The age of initiative
articles.snippet: We’re unprepared. In high school, the quarterback isn’t allowed to call the plays, the actor isn’t allowed to write the lines and the math whiz isn’t allowed to choose what to prove. We all grew up in the age of compliance (and indoctrination). The long tail of the internet and the astonishing leverage of AI has made this training much less valuable. No matter what you do for a living, there’s a machine standing by, waiting for instructions. Instructions from you, if you choose, or from your overlords if you don’t. And following the playbook isn’t much help, because the world is changing so fast, a playbook is obsolete by the time someone hands it to you. One reason AI got such a fast start is that it gave people seeking compliance a chance to wait for the AI to tell them what to do next. Quick, cheap answers. AI gives bosses a cheaper (and often more compliant) alternative to hiring humans to do some tasks. For those indoctrinated to comply, this is stressful. The stress is due to a desire to get things back to normal, to give them a chance to comply again, but right here, right now, is as normal as things are ever going to get. “Good jobs” are no longer sinecures where success comes from following instructions. It’s an abrupt change, and winging it is insufficient. Handling this sudden transition alone is too difficult. But we have a chance to find the others, to connect and be part of a cohort that challenges, educates and encourages each other on the path to find a way forward. We accepted that it was required to spend years being trained to handle a life of compliance. Now we have the chance to lean into the hard work we’ll need to do to thrive in an age of initiative.

articles.snippet: At GTC Berlin, banks, payment companies and financial data providers are showing what production-scale intelligence looks like — built on NVIDIA accelerated computing, powered by open weight models and running on their own infrastructure. PRAGMA answers that,” said Pavel Nesterov, head of AI at Revolut. “Built in collaboration with NVIDIA, it’s the clearest proof yet that the gap between a research breakthrough and a production banking system can be closed.” Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Training on Accelerated Infrastructure Starling Bank , the first bank to train an agentic model on U.K. sovereign cloud infrastructure, has developed “Starling Intelligence” — the intelligence layer that underpins its AI capability — on Civo’s U.K. cloud using the bank’s own transaction data. Lloyds Banking Group built ATUM , a transaction foundation model that converts billions of banking transactions into reusable intelligence — accelerated with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and improving efficiency across bank-wide use cases. SBS launched a banking sovereign intelligence platform so banks can run generative and agentic models without their data leaving their own walls. Open Models at a Fraction of the Cost Open weight models give European financial institutions proprietary intelligence built on data they own, at costs they control. NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform is the engine running beneath them. Neobank bunq’s agentic assistant Finn now runs on open weight models. Powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, deploying on Nebius matches the quality of leading closed models at 60% of the cost per answer. NatWest is building technology designed to recognize the full range of British accents, dialects and financial terminology, developed with NVIDIA’s speech models, including Nemotron 3.5 ASR. Modulr is building specialized models for distinct parts of payment operations, based on the NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B open model. Santander is an early adopter of the new NVIDIA Kumo family of open weight foundation models for structured financial data, using them to build specialized intelligence for core banking workloads. Accelerated Computing Transforms Financial Research LSEG is working with NVIDIA to help financial institutions analyze large volumes of historical tick data up to 10x faster with the Polars GPU engine , accelerated by NVIDIA cuDF on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. RavenPack built a dataset generation pipeline on Bigdata.com that takes a plain-language research hypothesis and returns a labeled, backtest-ready dataset — running on a fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron model. Investors can use these datasets to identify, analyze and visualize market trends. Speeding Data Pipelines to Improve Fraud Detection RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs and NVIDIA cuDF help accelerate data processing across multi-terabyte-scale, siloed, regulated sources, compressing the time from data to decision for fraud and other scenarios. HSBC provides near-real-time client insights that support customer processes and on-demand decision-making while minimizing risk and fraud, powered by 5x faster data processing on Starburst Enterprise’s GPU Engine . articles.snippet: To help developers rapidly build world models , which help physical AI systems understand and simulate the real world, NVIDIA has expanded the Cosmos platform with new training tools, simulation checkpoints and Cosmos Data Factory blueprints. Ranking top five on six different open models leaderboards, the NVIDIA Cosmos platform gives world model builders the frontier open models — as well as data, training and optimization tools and recipes — to scale training data, adapt models, test behavior and optimize for performance before deployment. Build Better Training Data Building world models begins with multimodal, multisensory data. NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory brings together the tools and skills for labeling, curating, augmenting and evaluating data at scale for training physical AI. Cosmos Curator, a GPU-accelerated solution for curating video training datasets, has now added support for multimodal multisensory inputs and processing blocks. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Cosmos Data Factory now offers the following five cloud-native blueprints and is available through GitHub , Microsoft Azure , Nebius and CoreWeave : Autonomous Vehicle Dataset Generation: Curates and labels driving data, then adds synthetic examples of hard-to-capture scenarios to expand training coverage. Image Attribute Augmentation: Varies object appearance to improve image search. Event Video Generation: Turns still images into synthetic videos of rare or unsafe events. Defect Image Generation: Generates printed circuit board, metal and glass defect images for inspection models. Video Data Augmentation: Changes weather and lighting in existing footage while preserving scene structure. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/CDF-visual-Oct20.mp4 Cosmos Data Factory accelerates data curation, processing and synthetic data generation with agentic skills. Companies are already putting Cosmos Data Factory blueprints to work to speed their physical AI development workflows. This is expected to reduce repeated physical test drives by up to 90% and shorten development cycle times by up to 85%. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Porche-Cosmos-Data-Factory.mp4 Porsche searching and augmenting autonomous vehicle data footage in Voxel51, powered by Cosmos Data Factory. Ultralytics , a computer vision company, retrained its YOLO model with real images and targeted synthetic defects generated using Cosmos Data Factory, improving defect localization and recall. Developers and agents can now adapt open models like GR00T , Alpamayo , QWEN, Pi0.5 and other compatible Hugging Face models through fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, optimize the model with distillation and quantization, and deploy with high-performing inference. Cosmos Framework is an open, modular framework of model training and optimization tools and skills to accelerate world model development. To develop a world model specialized for egocentric manipulation, robotics research lab MicroAGI post-trained Cosmos 3 on videos of humans manipulating objects and distilled its 32-billion-parameter reasoner down to an 8-billion-parameter Nano model with no loss in accuracy. Developers can label data and post-train Cosmos 3 on Roboflow for their specific environments and tasks, then deploy those models to RoboFlow hosted or on-premises NVIDIA GPUs to bring video reasoning into factories and warehouses. articles.title: How Companies Are Using NVIDIA DSX to Break the Power Bottleneck
articles.snippet: Companies around the world are building on the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run the grid and the AI factory as one system, from the substation to the rack. Their adoption of the platform responds to an acute problem. Power is now the biggest bottleneck in infrastructure. More than $300 billion in equipment is backlogged, and over 200 gigawatts of projects are waiting in U.S. interconnection queues. One root cause of the bottleneck is siloed systems. The grid, the facility and the compute inside have long been designed independently from one another, creating the conditions for delays, risk and stranded capacity. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements To help address this, NVIDIA DSX brings these systems together: NVIDIA DSX Sim and SimReady assets from leading energy manufacturers let engineers simulate the grid, substation and AI factory together, validating generators, switchgear, power systems and cooling before breaking ground. NVIDIA DSX Flex syncs AI factory demand with grid conditions and onsite generation, turning AI factories from static loads into flexible grid assets. NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS and DSX Exchange squeeze more compute from every watt and securely share signals across compute, networking, energy, cooling and operations. GE Vernova is deploying its grid-to-facility and rack power expertise to complement NVIDIA DSX systems, enabling customers to transform power constraints into competitive advantages while maximizing compute and token output, sustainability and grid reliability. Hitachi Energy ’s battery energy storage system has qualified as NVIDIA DSX Ready , helping customers identify power infrastructure that meets applicable NVIDIA DSX reference architecture design requirements for resilient, reliable and scalable AI factories. Schneider Electric , together with AVEVA and ETAP, is advancing NVIDIA DSX with validated NVIDIA Vera Rubin power and cooling reference architectures and an NVIDIA Omniverse -powered AI factory digital twin. Combining AVEVA ’s engineering software expertise with NVIDIA SimReady assets, OpenUSD and Omniverse enables connecting simulations, real-time operational data and AI-driven optimization across AVEVA, Schneider Electric and third-party solutions. Together, these capabilities help organizations design, simulate, operate and optimize data centers across their lifecycle, improving energy efficiency and workload performance while accelerating time to token. Siemens Energy is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA by developing a reference design for resilient, scalable and grid-aware power infrastructure across power generation, transmission and distribution. This design is aligned with the requirements of the NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin AI factory design. The company is also exploring usingNVIDIA technologies such as RAPIDS, Metropolis and Isaac Sim for its Noedra digital twin platform, evaluating how the technologies could enhance grid infrastructure monitoring, identify emerging risks and support unplanned outage prevention. Phaidra integrated DSX Flex, DSX Max-Q and DSX Exchange into its self-learning agents, optimizing cooling and power allocation to maximize tokens per watt, improve grid flexibility and deliver about 10% more compute within the same power envelope. Emerald AI integrated its Conductor platform into DSX Flex to help utilities tap underused grid capacity, an approach modeled to unlock up to 100 gigawatts on the existing U.S. grid. articles.title: NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations
articles.snippet: European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin. Frontier Results With Open Models Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open and frontier models to advance agentic commerce, digital product discovery and retail R&D. Shopify post-trains open models to reach frontier-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Its engineers use the NVIDIA Megatron Bridge library for faster fine-tuning and NVIDIA NeMo RL for reinforcement learning. Shopify has post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements On Shopify’s internal benchmark, the post-trained model surpasses a leading frontier model in accuracy while cutting serving costs by 90% and delivering responses 7x faster. Beyond Sidekick, NVIDIA CCluster vLLM inference optimization software helped Shopify achieve 4.5x faster performance and up to 12x lower inference cost across five additional use cases: catalog enrichment, merchant assistant, e-commerce shopping simulation, product taxonomy classification, and merchant and buyer recommendations. Zooplus , Europe’s leading online pet retailer, with Infosys and NVIDIA technologies rebuilt its product discovery stack for the agentic era. A production ready prototype deployed inside Zooplus ’ Amazon Web Services (AWS) environment achieved 86% search accuracy using the NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever library for semantic search and the NVIDIA Blueprint for retail catalog enrichment for generated, search-ready product attributes. Photoroom results from its deployment with Vestiaire Collective , where its Image Editing API now standardizes every primary image, about 40,000 a day across 70 countries, at the point of listing. Listings processed by Photoroom sold at a 5% higher rate of liquidity, with 3% to 7% more unique views per product page . The pipeline runs on NVIDIA GPUs with TensorRT and Triton Inference Server, and NVIDIA Dynamo Snapshot can help users quickly respond to demand spikes. Omi launched ProductDrop, a workflow that anchors every generated image to an approved digital twin, letting brands scale creative output across entire catalogs without introducing product errors . L’Oréal is using this approach, combining Omi ’s digital twins with generated brand environments within its CreAItech program. Omi runs TRELLIS 3D asset generation on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, speeding up inference by 10x and reducing pipeline latency by 4x. In addition, L’Oréal is accelerating the discovery of the best ingredient combinations, moving from months of experimentation to hours of computational screening, with the integration of NVIDIA ALCHEMI into its research workflow. L’Oréal is also testing this approach with CurieOS, Orbital Industries ‘ operating system for science and engineering, using OrbMol-v2, its open source molecular simulation model. Integrated with the NVIDIA ALCHEMI Toolkit and powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, OrbMol-v2 is five times faster than comparable models and delivers 21% lower error than the next-best model of its kind. This AI-based workflow enables researchers to identify the most promising ingredient combinations for solubilizing UV filters and optimizing performance before committing to laboratory testing. Mirakl , a software company for intelligent commerce, runs open models on NVIDIA GPUs, both on its own infrastructure and through European cloud providers like Scaleway . This keeps its technology sovereign, avoids vendor lock-in and delivers the speed and scale its customers expect . Mirakl ’s Catalog Transformer pairs fine-tuned open models with proprietary services and has onboarded more than 70 million products, turning messy vendor data into accurate, well-organized catalogs. Physical Intelligence Enables Training in Simulation NVIDIA physical AI, digital twins and open models help simulate retail environments, automate warehouse operations and deliver virtual try-on experiences for European retailers and fashion brands. Otto Group advanced its autonomous warehouse under human supervision initiative — built with Reply on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and running on Google Cloud — to the group’s largest fulfillment center in Haldensleben, Germany. New capabilities let logistics teams design, test and optimize warehouse operations entirely in simulation before any physical implementation . ALLSIDES launched its 3D Digital Twin Factory: an automated pipeline that transforms physical objects into SimReady 3D digital twins in minutes, capturing sub-millimeter geometric accuracy, measured physical properties and fully relightable materials that maintain accuracy under any lighting condition. Those digital twins serve as the foundation for simulating entire store layouts in 3D, as well as for tracking products reliably throughout the shopping journey and at checkout regardless of ambient light. Built on NVIDIA CUDA, OptiX and TensorRT, the platform already serves brands including adidas , Amazon , Nike , Zalando and Zara . CATCHES achieved production results from its RealFit deployment with AMIRI of conversion up 55%, add-to-cart up 80% and gross sales up 56% , all after seasonal adjustment against like-for-like styles. The company launched PredictiveFit, extending physics-based virtual try-on to retailers, as well as CASI, a personal fashion agent that shops, styles and sizes for customers over WhatsApp, powered by open weight models including NVIDIA Nemotron 3, built on NVIDIA Omniverse and the Newton Physics Engine. articles.title: Pioneers Across Europe Deploy NVIDIA Earth-2 Open Models to Power Real-World Weather and Climate Prediction
articles.snippet: Weather forecasts shape more than daily plans; timely weather information is crucial for energy producers, insurers and transport operators to plan around changing conditions. A global forecast can show a storm taking shape, but decisions about solar farms, shipping routes or insured property depend on what happens locally. NVIDIA Earth-2 gives developers and researchers a family of open AI models and tools they can customize with their own data. Running on NVIDIA computing, these technologies support global weather prediction, detailed regional forecasts and environmental research. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements StormScope EU is the latest model to join Earth-2 — a regional version of the StormScope model for short-term forecasting, trained over Europe weather and climate data. It uses EUMETSAT satellite observations to predict evolving cloud conditions across 16 Meteosat channels at 10-minute intervals. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is showcasing a live StormScope EU pipeline in an interactive weather demo built in partnership with Earthmover . The demo uses Earth2Studio to run forecasts and Earthmover’s data platform to manage and serve the real-time results, which are updated as soon as new satellite observations come in, every 10 minutes. Earthmover serves these results as map tiles, letting visitors explore predictions across Europe without downloading entire datasets. Developers can combine Earth-2 models in workflows tailored to regional needs, using StormScope for short-term forecasting and CorrDiff to add local detail to coarser weather data. Developers can also pick up these model architectures and train them for new environmental applications such as air-quality modeling. The open source NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo framework provides training and customization tools so teams can build applications that incorporate proprietary data and domain expertise to meet regional needs. Organizations building on Earth-2 capabilities include: AXA is using NVIDIA Earth-2’s FourCastNet 3 to study regional cyclone risk beyond the historical record across more than 1,000 simulated seasons, generating insights that can inform risk assessments and help customers target prevention efforts. Vaisala Xweather is combining Earth-2 with its proprietary observations , lightning data and forecasting expertise to enhance its weather intelligence platforms for government, energy, maritime, transportation and insurance customers. Its work includes adapting StormScope with lightning data to advance short-term forecasting lead time and make these warnings accessible through Vaisala Xweather’s software-as-a-service offerings and AI-assistant integrations. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Vaisala-Xweather-Nvidia-StormScope.mp4 Video courtesy of Vaisala Xweather. University of Manchester researchers adapted the Earth-2 CorrDiff model for U.K. air-quality modeling. It trained the model on the NVIDIA-powered Isambard-AI supercomputer and ran it locally on NVIDIA DGX Spark systems, bringing environmental modeling from a national supercomputer to the desktop. TotalEnergies is exploring NVIDIA Earth-2 for solar-energy forecasting, evaluating StormScope-based solar-radiation nowcasts at two photovoltaic sites and developing models to provide weather information at subhourly intervals. The work explores how more detailed forecasts could help anticipate changes in solar-power generation. Space42 developed SARDiff4Height using CorrDiff and NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo. The research estimates surface heights from a single radar image and produces uncertainty maps, helping analysts understand where estimates need closer scrutiny. Explore NVIDIA Earth-2 open models and tools , and explore with Earth2Studio’s forecasting examples . Read AXA’s hurricane-risk case study and Manchester’s air-quality story to learn how teams are adapting weather AI to specialized challenges. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements

articles.title: Toward depth
articles.snippet: Juan Tamariz and Wendell Berry recently passed away. Between them, they had more than 170 years of generous contribution. Juan was a card magician. His students are generally considered the best working in the world today. Wendell was a farmer and a writer. His essays on non-industrial farming and community-building will resonate for generations. What each had in common was the patience and commitment to choose depth. To seek out the inconvenient path because it mattered. Neither traded for easily measured metrics or convenience. Instead, they chose a path and followed it, leaving things better than they found them. Looking back a century, it’s easy to appreciate this. And yet, each and every day, it requires a recommitment. “Under the circumstances,” it’s tempting to justify the small compromises that corrode our work. The hard part is to realize that we’re not under the circumstances; we are them. We can start today.
